title: Per-tenant capability-attestation logs ship as MCP framework default by Q4 2026
body: By Q4 2026 the May 9 capability-attestation convergence forces signed per-tenant capability-attestation logs out of the Anthropic-specific Project Glasswing posture and into the default control-plane primitive shipped by every major MCP-server framework and hyperscaler-managed agentic-AI runtime. The catalysts that land in a single weekend cycle are concrete and mutually reinforcing: a Saturday arxiv preprint (2605.05933) by MIT CSAIL, ETH Zurich, and Anthropic provides a formal-verification framework for per-tenant capability attestation over MCP tool-call graphs and proves a no-cross-tenant-information-leakage property under the gating composition rule, giving downstream framework maintainers a citable safety theorem rather than a hand-waved design pattern; Microsoft Defender for Cloud's MCP-server threat-detection module now quarantines 24 percent of net-new MCP servers seen on Defender-protected estates within the first 30 minutes of provisioning, up from 19 percent the day before, demonstrating that the unattested control-plane surface is the operational attack surface; Cisco-Astrix's MCP-server identity gateway (co-branded with Defender XDR plus the Microsoft Agent 365 audit ledger) reaches 740 enterprise-tenant deployments inside its first 48 hours, signalling that the demand-side has moved past pilots; Sysdig Threat Research's weekend addendum reports median time-from-MCP-server-provisioning to first credential-extraction-attempt has fallen to 19 minutes on unprotected estates versus 4.3 hours on Defender-protected tenants, putting a measurable cost on the absence of attestation; and the Microsoft Azure AI Foundry Skill Catalog plus AWS Bedrock Agent Registry plus Google Cloud Vertex AI Agent Governance Center weekend updates extend signed-skill-provenance and reciprocity-attestation surface across all three hyperscaler-managed agentic runtimes within 48 hours of the Anthropic and OpenAI registry launches. The structural force is that once a peer-reviewed leakage-freedom proof exists for the gating composition rule, framework maintainers can cite the theorem rather than ship bespoke audit logic, and the Defender plus Sysdig telemetry numbers convert the question from policy to procurement. The most likely shape is a per-tenant attestation-log primitive added as a first-class object in the modelcontextprotocol reference server, the FastMCP Python framework, the LangChain MCP adapter, the LlamaIndex MCP toolkit, and the three hyperscaler agent registries, with default schemas for capability scope, tenant identity, gating-rule composition trace, and a verifiable-event chain that holds up to the audit-trail review Simon Willison flagged Saturday. Sovereign-cloud and FedRAMP-Moderate tenants adopt it first because the Mythos-class capability gating is already a procurement gate. Bear case is a competing framework refusing the composition rule and forking the schema; absent that, Q4 2026 lands signed per-tenant attestation logs as the documented default across the cohort.

reasoning.given: Defender quarantines 24% of new MCP servers; Sysdig logs 19-min credential extraction unprotected.
reasoning.so_that: FastMCP, LangChain, LlamaIndex MCP toolkits + three hyperscaler registries ship per-tenant attestation logs by default.
reasoning.landing: By Q4 2026; sovereign-cloud + FedRAMP-Moderate tenants adopt first.
reasoning.plain_language: Researchers proved a way to log AI-agent permissions safely across tenants, so the main agent toolkits will copy that logging by default.

summary: A May 9 MIT CSAIL + ETH Zurich + Anthropic arxiv paper proves no-cross-tenant-leakage for per-tenant MCP capability gating, while Defender quarantines 24% of new MCP servers and Sysdig logs 19-min credential extraction. By Q4 2026 per-tenant attestation logs ship as MCP framework default.
